The provided documents detail the technical specifications, optimization campaigns, and user-facing documentation for **Strata**, a local inference engine designed to run large language models on consumer hardware. The core narrative focuses on a rigorous engineering effort to optimize performance on the **Intel Arc A770 GPU** using the SYCL backend, alongside broader product documentation for AMD and Intel architectures.

The primary technical document, `A770_SPEED_SPEC.md`, outlines a campaign to achieve at least 20 tokens/second (tok/s) decode speed for the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Coder model. The project began with a baseline of ~2.5 tok/s and progressed through several optimization phases. Initial efforts focused on "Work Package 1" (reliable event-based measurements) and "Work Package 2" (BF16 projection paths). Extensive benchmarking revealed that the BF16 projection kernels were not the bottleneck; the `STRATA_MMVF_ROWS` optimization was rejected as it slowed performance, and register tuning (`GRF`) yielded no gains.

The investigation shifted to "Work Package 3" and beyond, identifying that the decode window is dominated by **GPU-reach wait** (~71% of the time) and per-layer host-to-GPU synchronization.
